Hi Evan — great to meet today, and thanks for the clear asks. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap / recommended models to evaluate (initial shortlist):
1) Open model (open-source baseline): OpenLLaMA-3-13B (8-bit quant) — good match for concise generation and cost-friendly runs.
2) Mid-sized open variant: Falcon-7B-Instruct (int8 or dynamic quant) — faster throughput for high QPS.
3) Redwood proprietary baseline: RWD-13B-prop (our internal inference-optimized baseline) — this is the reference you compared against in the demo.

Why these: we picked an open large model + a smaller open model to understand the cost/quality slope, and included our optimized proprietary baseline so you can measure parity directly.

Suggested evaluation artifacts we'll share:
- Prompt set (the 120-case subset used in today's demo) — will attach as prompt-set-v1.txt.
- Eval harness + metrics (EM, BLEU for structured, and a 5-point human rating for helpfulness/accuracy) — we'll provide the runner and a short README.
- Example outputs CSV and a quick benchmark PDF summarizing token costs and latency per model.

Acceptance / parity guidance (proposal):
- Primary metric: human helpfulness/accuracy (5-point), target: >= 0.95x of your current baseline mean score.
- Secondary metric: exact-match (where applicable) or task F1, target: >= 0.9x of baseline.
- Latency: median p95 should be within 1.5x of baseline for online use, or we recommend Dedicated pool for tighter SLOs.

Next steps / timeline:
1) We'll drop the prompt set, harness, and a starter run (small sample outputs) by EOD today.
2) Your team runs the harness against the three models and shares we can help with ingest/outbound connectors if needed.
3) Reconvene next Tue (16 Mar) for a parity review + decision on expanding to 1k cases.

Attachments: prompt-set-v1.txt (attached), eval-harness-readme.md (link), sample-output.csv (we'll upload)

Let us know if you want to change the acceptance thresholds — we can make them stricter on a per-task basis.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Internal — evaluation design & acceptance details

Marissa / Lauren — summarizing the internal plan to support PayGrid's run and to make sure we align on metrics and artifacts we drop into the Drive (link below). I'll also coordinate infra credits / Dedicated trial if they need p95 latency parity.

Evaluation plan (internal checklist):
- Provide prompt-set-v1.txt (120 cases) + README with expected output format (CSV columns: case_id, prompt, baseline_output, candidate_output).
- Provide harness with blinded AB runner (we'll randomize order; each human judge sees de-identified outputs).
- Metric calc: compute mean of 5-pt helpfulness across judges; primary threshold: candidate_mean >= 0.95 * baseline_mean. Use trimmed mean (drop top/bottom 5%) to reduce outlier effect.
- Secondary: compute F1/EM on deterministic items; require candidate >= 0.9 * baseline.
- Reporting: generate summary PDF (open-vs-prop-benchmark.pdf) with per-case deltas and cost/latency table.

Infra support: if they need Dedicated to hit tighter latency SLOs, we can offer 2-week trial credits and help configure batching/quant profiles.

I'll upload the starter artifacts to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPayGridEval (owner: marissa_cole@redwood.ai). HubSpot: HS-123456.

Let me know if you want to tighten thresholds (e.g., 0.98x) or change trimming.

- Aditya
